steps.content: Several months have passed since Milly was formally admitted to the Bureau, and you've finally made your way back.
You've barely sat down at your desk when an interrogation request appears before you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I heard Milly's been settling in well. She's made a lot of friends among the Sinners, too... That's a relief.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I believe your arrangements have proven effective, Chief. There's no need to be too concerned.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Good afternoon, Chief. I'm so happy you've finally come to see me.
This is the first time you've properly seen her face-to-face since she woke up.
She sits relaxed in her chair and offers a smile as sweet as honey.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: It's been months since we parted on Euphoria. I've missed you so much.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Whenever I missed you, I'd ask the staff about you. They were always very kind and would tell me what you were up to. Whether you'd returned safely, whether you were hurt, or... I worried, but there wasn't much I could do.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I knew you were busy with important things, and that's why you couldn't come see me. So I tried my best to be patient.

steps.speaker: Option
options: I heard you've been doing well here.
I'm sorry it took me so long.

choices.text: I heard you've been doing well here.
I'm sorry it took me so long.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I have. There are so many interesting people in the Bureau. Thanks to them, every day has been rewarding.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you getting used to things here?

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Yes! There are so many interesting people in the Bureau. Thanks to them, every day has been rewarding.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I've talked about dance with Miss Hamel, and discussed the best donuts in Eastside with Miss Poffy. Miss Yugu always has fascinating stories about Eastia to share with me.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: There are other Sinners I've only seen in passing. We haven't had a chance to talk yet. But my next goal is to become friends with everyone.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Some might find life here boring, but coming from Euphoria, I'm used to being locked in one place. Besides, everyone at the Bureau is so much more interesting than the ones back there.
She pauses for a moment.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I... I've been trying my best to put into practice what Kawa-kawa, Zephyr, and you wanted to tell me.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I know what you've been trying to tell me: that I need to love myself before I can love others, and love the world before I can love all the people in it. I get the idea, and I've found many things I enjoy now, but... I think it would make me happier if I could share them with the person I love most.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: These precious memories... I want to share them with you, Chief.
Cautiously, she looks into your eyes.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Can I?

You can feel the intensity in her eyes. The rise and fall of her chest betrays the excitement she's trying so hard to contain. Her words are measured, her actions restrained. She doesn't want to make you uncomfortable, but the love she feels is threatening to spill.
You choose your words carefully.

steps.speaker: Option
options: I heard you ran into a sandstorm on your way back?

choices.text: I heard you ran into a sandstorm on your way back?

steps.content: Milly's expression brightens.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Yes. We were on the sand ship, and the captain said it was a huge, rare storm. It was so dangerous. All I could think was, if I died there, I'd never see you again. So I knew I had to be strong.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I climbed to the top of the mast—it was about to be blown away—and secured the transmitter. And there, I saw them. The giant moving dunes that they say you can only see in a sandstorm.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: It was breathtaking! The dunes rolled like colorful dragons. And the sand that flew into my hair... it was colored, too.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Kawa-kawa told me that the sand dunes and the stars are made of the same stuff. And that the most beautiful night sky is the one that comes after a sandstorm.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Then, I met Zephyr in DisCity. She took me to so many places. I tried melon from before the Nightfall and watched the latest blockbuster movie. We spent the entire night at the bar. Everyone here looks at me differently from those people did on Euphoria. They don't "love" me; they simply treat me as an equal, a person just like them.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Meeting them made me realize... I'm so glad I left that place. I'm so glad to be alive.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I didn't do much to help you. You did it all yourself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You never gave up on yourself, even when you were afraid. Not during the sandstorm, and not on that cruise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I never thought of you as someone who needed saving. You fought to survive in that hell on your own, and you had the courage to help others.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Having help is certainly important. But the greatest reason you're here right now is because you refused to give up on yourself.
Silence falls. Milly seems lost in thought.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: ...Do you really not know what it is, Chief? The reason I refused to give up, the reason I found the strength to live, no matter the hardship?

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Do you remember, Chief? That gang shootout in the West District?

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: You saved a girl in an alley on that rainy day. She came from nothing. Her parents were horrible people who sold her to a gang just because she had pretty, golden hair.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: She tried to run, many, many times, but they always caught her. And every time, they'd beat her senseless. All she could do was escape into her fantasies to numb the pain and heal the wounds. Eventually, she got so good at it that she could even use her fantasies to numb the men with the sticks. At least, enough to make the beatings hurt a little less.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Then one day, the revolution came. Rustfire swept through the West District, and the gangs were wiped out. She was finally free. She could escape and not be dragged back.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: But... she was so weak. She got hurt in the escape, and she couldn't keep up with the crowds. She ended up lying in a filthy alley in the rain, waiting for the monsters to come, waiting to die.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: So she retreated into her fantasies one last time. She dreamed that someone would come, someone who would love her and protect her. Someone who would give her a happy home, a happy life. She was dying. The least she could do was imagine his face before the end.
steps.female_content: You can count on me to have your backs! Go and fight them without worry!

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: And then... as if the heavens heard her plea, someone ran toward her, driving back the growling monsters with flashes of red light.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: With rain and blood blurring her vision, she couldn't make out her savior's face. All she could tell was that he had shoulder-length hair and smelled of blood and gunpowder. He carried her to safety and gave her a dagger for self-defense.
steps.female_content: With rain and blood blurring her vision, she couldn't make out her savior's face. All she could tell was that she had shoulder-length hair and smelled of blood and gunpowder. She carried her to safety and gave her a dagger for self-defense.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Then he was gone... he seemed so busy. The dagger he gave her was sharp. Sharp enough to slit the monsters' throats. Or her own.
steps.female_content: Then she was gone... she seemed so busy. The dagger she gave her was sharp. Sharp enough to slit the monsters' throats. Or her own.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: But in the end, she didn't bring the blade on herself. Because now she had the hope to live. She believed that just like all her other fantasies had come true in one way or another, this person had to be her fantasy come true, too. The one who would love her, protect her, and give her a happy life.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: But it was just a fantasy, wasn't it? A fantasy that carried me through so many hardships that... I started to believe it was real.
The sweet scent of honey fills your senses.
Something flutters in your chest, pulsing, surging, fighting to break free.
You seem to see Milly rise from her seat and walk toward you. She takes your hand and places it against her cheek.
Her eyes are wet, like a newborn fawn's. The air she breathes seems laced with the sweetness of honey.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I wanted so badly for it to be real...
She leans in with a delicate peck. Once isn't enough. She does it again.
First your nose, then your cheek, and finally a careful, tentative touch against your lips.
Yet she lingers there, afraid to go any further.
Her movements are shy and cautious, terrified of shattering this fragile dream.
You feel something wet on your face and realize—she's crying.
Both bitterness and sweetness pass from her lips to yours. It seems that only here, in this illusion, can she finally have what she's always wanted.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Hah...

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: ...Thank you, Chief.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Hmm... Just the reaction I expected.
(Paths converge)
The illusion fades. The power Milly released was so minimal that it could hardly be considered a threat, and the interrogation room's alarm remains silent.
She's back in her chair, a faint smile on her lips. Her eyes are glistening, as if on the verge of tears.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Thank you, Chief. For letting me have my dream.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Really? You're so kind, Chief. But you don't have to comfort me like this...
You take an unconscious step toward her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I remember that battle. I remember saving a girl with golden hair, the color of honey. Her smile was adorable, and she was brave. I knew she could protect herself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then, not long after, I saw her again. She had become brighter, more dazzling than before. She had survived, with the dagger I gave her. Not only had she survived, but she'd helped so many others survive, too.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But a part of me was always worried. Worried that she was just blinded by a crush, that her love would end up trapping her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But she proved me wrong. She showed me that she wouldn't be confined to a small corner. She's taking new steps, finding a bigger world, embracing a more beautiful life.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm sorry, Milly. This time, I was the one who was afraid.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm looking forward to the day you invite me out, whether it's to see the stars in WhiteSands, or to enjoy the food in Eastside. I'd be delighted to go with you.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Chief... why are you only saying these things now?

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I've already prepared myself for heartbreak! Do you have any idea how long I've spent readying myself for rejection? How many nights I cried?
Milly's face flushes red, her eyes welling up with angry tears.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: I thought you didn't care for me at all! I'm already prepared to win you over from scratch.

steps.speaker: Milly
steps.content: Forget it, I'm not taking you with me! I'm taking someone else! You can just stay here and work yourself to death for all I care!
You easily catch her flailing hand and, unfazed by her tantrum, hold it gently in yours.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright. When you find an even more special place to take me, we'll go then.
